Managing Partner

Raju Lalwani

Raju

Connecting people, markets and business expectations.

Raju connects what customers expect with what businesses deliver. His work in sales and customer service, in Japan and the United States, centres on understanding people, earning trust and developing lasting business relationships.

Emailraju@setuhashi.com

LinkedIn profile ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Experience he brings

Raju began his working life in Japan. In a bespoke tailoring business he checked finished suits before delivery against what customers had been promised; in a Japanese education company he explained programmes to prospective adult students in Japanese, signed up new students and later trained newer colleagues.

In the United States, he developed business customers across several regions for a maker of custom carpets produced in India. He translated what buyers specified into precise production instructions for weavers in India, standardized how clients chose colours, and coordinated imports and delivery.

His later work in retail and hospitality has centred on serving people across cultures and languages, including leading a guest-services team. Drawing on that lived experience, he also helps individuals and teams prepare to work with Japan: its business etiquette, communication and workplace expectations.

A personal connection across borders

Born and raised in Japan, Raju maintains a deep affection for its language, people and everyday life. His Indian heritage and years in the United States add perspectives that help him relate to people across different backgrounds.

His commitment to SetuHashi

These connections underpin Raju’s commitment to bringing Japanese and Indian businesses closer together. He brings understanding of Japanese customers and working practices, practical commercial experience and a relationship-centred approach. Working alongside Shyam and Mak, he helps businesses understand one another and build the confidence needed to explore opportunities together.

Selected experience

Examples from Raju’s individual professional experience outside SetuHashi. They are not work carried out by SetuHashi.

  • Developing a US market for products made in India

    Turning US buyers’ requirements into production instructions that teams in India could follow.

  • Building a Japanese clientele in US menswear retail

    Earning the trust of Japanese customers and turning it into repeat business.

  • Recruiting adult students in Japan and training colleagues

    Explaining an offer to Japanese customers in Japanese, and training colleagues.

  • Checking quality before delivery in bespoke tailoring

    Checking finished work against what customers in Japan had been promised.

  • Turning a guest request into a recurring group arrangement

    Structuring a commercial incentive around a clear customer commitment.

  • Automating guest follow-up and arrival instructions

    Designing automation that freed customer-service time for more productive work.
